mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points within a month signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending and economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE increases > 0.5pp, or if the correlation between UNRATE changes and 5-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downwards.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances when GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters, or if the correlation between GDPC1 growth and 60-day returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a month signals a strong supply-side response, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as it indicates robust economic activity and potential for higher corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO increases > 2%, or if the correlation between INDPRO growth and 20-day returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When both housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) decline simultaneously by more than 5% over two months, it signals a broad-based weakening in demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both decline > 5% in 2 months
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline > 5%, or if the joint effect of HOUST and RSAFS on 20-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An always-on signal where a high level of nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 160,000 indicates a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as it signals robust economic activity and consumer spending.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances when PAYEMS > 160,000, or if the correlation between PAYEMS levels and 5-day returns is not significantly positive (p > 005).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 3% and inflation (CPIAUCSL) is rising by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals a potential overheating economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate future monetary tightening.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 3% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 3% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5%, or if the joint effect of FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL on 60-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime-conditional signal where during a monetary tightening cycle, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals a supply-side contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO declines > 1% during a monetary tightening cycle, or if the correlation between INDPRO declines and 20-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during such periods.
